From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API - preliminary unit economics and example pricing

Hi Samir — putting some numbers behind Marissa’s request. Below are conservative Hosted API unit economics based on the model mix you described (80% standard, 20% large-summary calls). These are illustrative and we can tighten after we confirm average tokens and commit level.

Assumptions:
- Tokens billed = prompt + completion (total tokens).
- Avg tokens/request = 300; 30M tokens / month => ~100k requests/month.
- Peak TPS sizing: sustain 12 TPS, short bursts to 18 TPS.

Example Hosted API list rates (no commitment):
- Standard models: $20 / 1M tokens
- Large-summary models: $90 / 1M tokens

Weighted effective cost (80/20) = 0.8*20 + 0.2*90 = $38 / 1M tokens.
For 30M tokens => 30 * $38 = $1,140 / month.

Commit discounts (examples):
- 3-month commit: 10% off listed rates
- 12-month commit: 20% off listed rates

With a 12-month commit the effective $/1M = $30.4 => 30M tokens ~= $912/mo.

If your budget target is $15k- $35k / month, you’re well above these illustrative hosted costs for 30-50M tokens (even at list). If you expect growth beyond 100M tokens, we’d also model Dedicated capacity for predictable latency and capacity pricing.

I can put together a short table (low/expected/high) with line items and discount scenarios — Marissa, do you want me to add that to the PRD we send to Finlytics?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Pricing & Solutions | Redwood Inference
